messages:
Taylor (AE): starting POC thread for Orion Health. They want on-prem app -> Redwood Private. Main open questions: should TLS terminate at their edge or our ingress? Can we preserve client source IP for their ACLs? Firewall rule checklist + DNS/PrivateLink guidance. Also need cost delta if they require a static egress IP. Can NetOps + Solutions chime in?
Amy (Solutions): short answer: two common patterns: 1) Tunnel to customer TGW/edge -> TGW peering -> our Private VPC (keeps source IP visible); 2) Tunnel to our edge + use PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for service access. If they want full end-to-end TLS under their control, terminate at their edge and forward over IPsec. If they want our proxy features (SNI routing, L7 inspection), terminate at our ingress.
Jordan (NetOps): minimal firewall/ACL checklist for POC:
```
- outbound TCP 443 to Redwood control plane CIDRs (we'll provide exact list)
- outbound TCP 443 to the PrivateLink ENI CIDRs (if using PrivateLink)
- UDP 500 & UDP 4500 inbound/outbound for IPsec (if using site-to-site)
- allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to resolver for PrivateLink private DNS resolution
```
Note: if you NAT at your egress (NAT GW/EIP) you'll present a stable source IP. VPC Peering generally preserves original source IP, while some transit setups or NATs will not.
Taylor (AE): can you drop a sample SG/ACL snippet I can paste into the customer's ticket? Also need an initial CIDR we can use for the POC to open on our side.
Jordan (NetOps): sample snippet below (send as plain text to their infra team):
```
# Customer outbound SG (for POC)
- allow tcp:443 -> <redwood-control-plane-cidr>/32  # replace with provided CIDR list
- allow tcp:443 -> <redwood-privatelink-enis-cidr>/32 # if using interface endpoints
- allow udp:500,udp:4500 -> <our-edge-ip>/32 # IPsec tunnel port when terminating at our edge
- allow udp:53,tcp:53 -> <their-dns-resolver>/32 # for private DNS resolution
```
I'll also create an ephemeral test CIDR on our side: 198.51.100.0/30 for the POC (expires in 72h).
Amy (Solutions): pricing context: if customer NATs at their edge with an EIP/NATGW, cost is on their side: NAT GW data processing (~$0.045/GB typical) + per-hour NAT charges (region dependent). If they ask us to provide a static egress IP on Redwood side (managed option), we can include a monthly fee + bandwidth costs in the SOW. For a rough quick estimate: assume 2TB/month -> data processing ~ $90; exact numbers depend on region & transfer direction. I'll follow up with a line item in the quote.
Maria (Security): for their security questionnaire, expect asks for:
- network diagram showing tunnel/peering/privatelink flows
- TLS ciphers & cert chain we support; ability to do mTLS
- SOC2 report link, KMS key usage + rotation cadence
- logging: flow logs, request logs retention and access controls
We can provide a templated network diagram and sample mTLS config. Also confirm: if TLS terminated on their edge then our link between edges can be IPsec + inner TLS if they request double-wrapped.
Taylor (AE): actionable items: 1) Jordan: paste SG/ACL + confirm ephemeral CIDR details. 2) Amy: add static-egress-ip managed option and rough per-GB estimate into quote. 3) Maria: draft short answers + attach SOC2 link + sample network diagram. I'll book a 30min handoff with their infra lead for tomorrow 10am.
Jordan (NetOps): done — ephemeral CIDR 198.51.100.0/30 created; SG snippet above copied to ticket.
Amy (Solutions): queued a pricing line item: "Managed static egress IP (per-month) + bandwidth". I'll DM the exact numbers to Taylor.
deploy-bot: test endpoint created: 10.2.150.88 for POC (lifecycle: 72h).
Taylor (AE): thanks team. I'll send this to the customer and confirm the 10am call. :thumbsup:
